sentences.text: I have been working on this software project since last morning.
sentences.hint: Use 'have been' with '-ing' verb for actions starting in past and continuing now.

sentences.text: Neither the manager nor the employees were present at the meeting.
sentences.hint: When using 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('employees').

sentences.text: I am adept at solving complex algorithmic problems under tight deadlines.
sentences.hint: 'Adept at' means highly skilled or proficient.

sentences.text: I possess a strong foundation in computer science and data structures.
sentences.hint: Speak clearly with steady pacing and natural pause after 'science'.

sentences.text: The candidate demonstrated remarkable resilience despite encountering unexpected technical bottlenecks.
sentences.hint: Focus on pronouncing 'remarkable resilience' and 'bottlenecks' distinctly.

sentences.text: We must streamline our deployment pipeline to mitigate potential security vulnerabilities.
sentences.hint: 'Streamline' means make more efficient; 'mitigate' means lessen severity.

sentences.text: If I had known about the campus drive earlier, I would have applied immediately.
sentences.hint: Use 'had + past participle' in if-clause and 'would have + past participle' in result.

sentences.text: Object-oriented programming optimizes code reusability through inheritance and encapsulation.
sentences.hint: Emphasize technical terms 'inheritance' and 'encapsulation' with clear pauses.

sentences.text: I would like to add a complementary perspective to what my peer just highlighted.
sentences.hint: 'Complementary perspective' politely introduces a new supporting argument in GD.

sentences.text: She has been working as a software developer at Google for three years.
sentences.hint: Use 'for' when specifying the total duration of time ('three years').
